The system had grown fast. Speed was prioritized over structure - until it wasn’t.
By the time performance became a problem, the backend had 14+ microservices.
In practice:
Auth logic duplicated across 6 services

Each service maintained its own DB connection pool

A single request triggered 4–5 internal API hops

Middleware inconsistently applied

articles.author: Jinwen Hao
articles.description:
Hi everyone!
We’ve all been there: You just need to trim a 30-second ringtone, crop a podcast intro, or clean up a voice memo. You search for an "Online Audio Cutter," only to find tools that:
Force you to create an account.
Slap a watermark on the file (how do you even watermark audio?!).
Hide the "Download" button behind a subscription paywall.
I got tired of the "fake free" tools, so over the last two weeks, I built Audio Cut — a dead-simple, professional-grade audio trimmer that stays out of your way.
💡 The Gap in the Market
I wanted to build a product that follows three "No's":
No Sign-ups: Go from landing page to download in 3 clicks.
No Quality Loss: High-fidelity processing that respects your original bitrate.
No Distractions: A clean, dark-mode UI focused entirely on the waveform.
🚀 Key Features for Power Users
Frame-Accurate Trimming: Zoom into the waveform to find the exact millisecond between words.
Instant Preview: Hear exactly what your cut sounds like before you export.
Multi-Format Support: Whether it’s an MP3, AAC, WAV, or OGG, we handle the conversion for you.
Privacy First: Your files are processed securely and deleted from our temporary storage immediately after conversion.
🛠️ Why This Product Exists
I focused on Speed and Reliability. By optimizing the backend processing, Audio Cut can handle large files (like 1-hour podcast raw tapes) that usually crash standard browser-based editors. We’ve moved the heavy lifting to our optimized servers so your browser stays fast and responsive.
📈 What’s Next?
Batch Processing: Trim 10 files at once.
Fade In/Out Effects: For smoother transitions.
Audio Extraction: Stripping audio from video URLs directly.
🌍 Give it a Spin!
👉 https://audiocut.net (Insert your actual URL)
I’d love to hear from you: What is the one "small" audio task that always feels harder than it should be? Let me know in the comments, and I might build a tool for it next!
articles.title: Stop Fighting With Paid Tools: I Launched a 100% Free Online Audio Cutter ✂️

articles.author: Gokul Skumar
articles.description:
What is the Loki Stack?


Loki Stack is a lightweight, cloud‑native logging system built with the same design philosophy as Prometheus. It’s a great fit for Kubernetes environments because it keeps things simple, scalable, and cost‑effective — all of which matter a lot in modern DevOps workflows.
Unlike traditional logging tools that index the entire log content, Loki takes a smarter approach: it indexes only the metadata labels. Logs themselves are stored as compressed streams. This makes Loki far more efficient and cheaper to run compared to systems like Elasticsearch.
The core engine. It handles log ingestion, storage, and querying. Components like the Distributor, Ingester, and Querier work together to push logs, compress them, store them (often in S3 or GCS), and make them searchable.…

articles.author: williamandresr
articles.description:
If you use uv on Windows and your projects live in OneDrive, you've probably already run into the problem: OneDrive tries to sync the .venv folder and everything breaks — slow sync, locked files, corrupted environments.
The solution is to centralize virtual environments outside of OneDrive and have uv use them automatically.
uv creates the virtual environment inside each project:
OneDrive/
└── dev/
    └── my-project/
        ├── .venv/          ← OneDrive tries to sync this
        └── pyproject.toml

A typical .venv folder contains thousands of small files. OneDrive doesn't know to ignore them and syncs everything, causing slowdowns, conflicts, and sometimes corrupted environments.
Centralize environments outside of OneDrive using the UV_PROJECT_ENVIRONMENT environment variable:
C:\Users…
